Contracts need offer, acceptance and consideration. The common law mirror image rule means any change is a rejection. However the UCC applies to goods and section 2-207 relaxes that rule, so the confirmation likely formed a contract despite the delivery date change, which is a mere proposal. Marlow was silent so the March 20 term is not part of the deal, and the late delivery may be a breach by Quill, but the buyer would need to show it is material.
